title: B1-24 · Review, simulation and profile for skill

blocks.text: B1-24 · Review, simulation and profile for skill
Lesson overview

The last three weeks of the level serve to consolidate, measure and decide where to work. There's no new grammar. In the first week you review the vocabulary for areas and the grammar framework of B1 and reread the units; in the second, do a complete simulation of the exam , with new texts and in real conditions; in the third build your profile for skills and work on gaps that the simulation showed. In the week 156 support the exam B1 (Part IV).

rows: 14–16 hours · three weeks (weeks 153–155 of the calendar), plus the exam in the week 156; EGY-10 continues in its separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials All volume, Appendix B (lexic), Reference grammar (Part VI), error book, progress log, a native language tutor for oral simulation
Targets. At the end of the three weeks:
1. recognize and use vocabulary B1 of the fifteen areas of the section 2;
2. recognize without hesitation the structures of the grammatical framework of the section 3;
3. read silently a no-voice news of about 200 words at least 70 words per minute and refer to content;
4. you understand a news and radio interview on well-known topics and write a dictation with at least the85% of words correct;
5. translate journalistic and administrative phrases into English with precision (Accessories at least 3/4);
6. write a summary of 100–120 words and a formal letter of 120–150 words;
7. support 20 minutes of interview in fuṣḥā and 4 minutes in Egyptian;
8. know your skill profile and you know which units to review before the exam.
Three-week plan.

Important. Do not read sections 6–10 before the simulation: the texts are new on purpose, because the simulation measures what you can do in front of a text you have never seen.
1. How to Review

• Active recall. Each unit has an active recall section: cover the right column and Pick up aloud. Make the units tables that the log marks as weakest; for the vocabulary use Appendix B covering the Arabic column.

• Notebook of errors. Copy the correct errors of the four module tests, grouped by type (agreement, cases, reading without vowels, register, translation). Read them every day of the week 153: are the mistakes you are most likely to repeat.
• No vowels. Read the readings of the units B1.3 and B1.4 without looking at the translation; For vocating texts Units B1.1 and B1.2, cover the vowels with a sheet.
• Register. Note in the log the simulation scores by section: they are the base of the profile (section 11)
and the plan of the week 155.
• Tutor. Oral simulation should be done with a native speaker: pronunciation and interaction do not self-evaluate.
The Egyptian part needs an Egyptian speaker.
2. The vocabulary B1 by areas
The keywords of each area, with the units where you studied them. The complete list is in Appendix B.

⁧هل ما زلنا بحاجة إلى المكتبات العامة؟⁩
⁧يتساءل كثيرون اليوم: لماذا نذهب إلى المكتبة إذا كان بإمكاننا أن نقرأ أي كتاب على الشاشة؟ ويرى⁩
⁧أصحاب هذا الرأي أن المكتبات أصبحت مكانا للماضي، وأن على الدولة أن تنفق أموالها على الإنترنت بدلا⁩
⁧من المباني والرفوف.⁩
⁧غير أن الأرقام تقول شيئا آخر. فبحسب استطلاع أجرته وزارة الثقافة العام الماضي، ارتفع عدد زوار⁩
⁧المكتبات العامة في المدن الكبرى بنسبة خمسة عشر بالمئة خلال ثلاث سنوات. ويعود ذلك، كما يوضح⁩
⁧الاستطلاع، إلى أن المكتبة لم تعد مجرد مكان لاستعارة الكتب، بل أصبحت مركزا للحياة الثقافية: ففيها⁩
⁧تنظم دورات في اللغات والحاسوب، وأمسيات شعرية، ونشاطات للأطفال، كما يجد فيها الطلاب مكانا هادئا⁩
⁧للدراسة.⁩
⁧ومن جهة أخرى، تؤدي المكتبة دورا اجتماعيا مهما. فكبار السن الذين يعيشون وحدهم يجدون فيها من⁩
⁧يتحدثون إليه، والمهاجرون الجدد يتعلمون فيها لغة البلد، والأسر التي لا تملك حاسوبا تستعمل أجهزتها⁩
⁧مجانا.⁩
⁧ولا يعني ذلك أن المكتبات لا تواجه مشكلات. فميزانياتها تتراجع في كثير من البلدان، وبعضها يغلق أبوابه⁩
⁧في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع، وهو الوقت الذي يحتاج فيه الناس إليها أكثر. لذلك يدعو الخبراء إلى تطوير⁩
⁧المكتبات بدلا من إغلاقها، عن طريق إضافة الخدمات الرقمية إلى الكتب الورقية، وفتح أبوابها في المساء.⁩
⁧وفي الختام، يمكن القول إن المكتبة العامة ليست مبنى مليئا بالكتب القديمة، بل هي بيت مفتوح للجميع،⁩
⁧وإن الاستثمار فيها استثمار في المجتمع كله.⁩

10. Simulation · E Oral (20 points)

With the tutor, about 22 minutes. The tutor has the texts and indications in the solutions; You don't make them. E1 · Reading aloud and questions (3 minutes). Read a short text without vowels that you have never seen; The tutor timers and then asks you two questions about the content. E2 · Spontaneous conversation (5 minutes). The tutor chooses two of your topic tabs (B1-23) and converse with you at normal speed. Ask for clarification, verification, take time, motivate the answers, ask at least two questions. E3 - Discussion (4 minutes). The tutor offers you a theme (library and digital; TV series to learn languages; voluntary work; living in a big city): give your opinion, argue with two reasons and an example, answer the objections, and eventually summarize the two positions. E4 · Report a report (3 minutes). The tutor reads a short story twice. Refer to it in Arabic with the attribution formulas ( ⁧ذَكَرَتْ⁩ …, ⁧قَالَ⁩ … ⁧إِنَّ⁩ …, ⁧بِحَسَبِ⁩ ...), distinguishing who says what. E5 · Egyptian (4 minutes, 5 points). The tutor is an Egyptian friend. You are at the bar: orders for both (EGY-08); then you talk about a movie or a series that you saw (EGY-10): you give your opinion, he disagrees, and eventually propose to see you again (EGY-05). Evaluation. Fuṣḥā (E1–E4, 15 points): Accuracy 1–5 + Fluidity and interaction 1–5 + Pronunciation and register 1–5. Egyptian (E)5, 5 points): Effectiveness 1–5 (Task done, Egyptian without forms of fuṣḥā, intelligible pronunciation). At least 2 in every criterion.

blocks.text: 14. Ready for the exam?
Each entry will be checked before the week 156.
1. I passed the four module tests (or repeated them with the tutor).
2. In the simulation I have at least 12/20 in each section, or I did the recovery indicated by the profile.
3. I read silently a word without vowels at least 70 words per minute.
4. My dictation has at least the85% of correct words.
5. In the translation I have at least 3/4 of Accuracy and I make the degree of certainty ( ⁧زَعَمَ⁩ , ⁧يُرَجَّحُ⁩ , ⁧قَدْ⁩ ).
6. I can write with memory opening, greeting, request and closing of a formal letter.
7. I know the formulas of the summary and the checklist of B1-21.
8. I have at least six topics ready for the oral.
9. In Egyptian I can order, solve a practical problem and say what I think of a movie.
10. I've set up the tutor for the two half-days of the exam, and I'm ready to read the scripts.
